## Abstract

Influential existing research has suggested that rather than being static, mortality declines decelerate at young ages and accelerate at old ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Without accounting for this feature, the forecast mortality rates of the popular Lee–Carter (LC) model are less reliable in the long run.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To provide more accurate mortality forecasting, we introduce a time-varying coefficients extension of the LC model by adopting the effective kernel methods.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: With two frequently used kernel functions, Epanechnikov (LC-E) and Gaussian (LC-G), we demonstrate that the proposed extension is easy to implement, incorporates the rotating patterns of mortality decline and is straightforwardly extensible to multi-population cases.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Using a large sample of 15 countries over 1950–2019, we show that LC-E and LC-G, as well as their multi-population counterparts, can consistently improve the forecasting accuracy of the competing LC and Li–Lee models in both single- and multi-population scenarios.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Introduction

The ongoing improvement of human life expectancy around the world has far-reaching influences on many aspects of our society.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For instance, Maestas et al. [1] highlight the importance of considering demographic changes, including mortality projections, in analyzing labor supply.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mortality projections are used to predict future changes in the size and age structure of the labor force, which can help inform policy decisions related to workforce development and training, immigration, and other factors that affect the labor market.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For the healthcare system, Fenton et al. [2] indicate the importance of considering changes in mortality projections in analyzing healthcare utilization and expenditure.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specifically, prediction of future demand for health and medical care services is dependent on mortality projections.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Such predictions may inform policy decisions related to the allocation of resources for healthcare and the design of related systems.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The importance of accurate mortality projections is also witnessed in retirement and pensions and the insurance industry (see, for example, ref. [3], among others).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: To better model the underlying patterns of mortality improvement is, therefore, essential to enhance accuracy of mortality projection.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Among the existing studies, Lee and Carter [4] is the mostly widely used factor-based mortality model, known as the LC model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite its popularity, the LC model assumes constant age-specific mortality decline speeds over time.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, the LC model produces increasingly large proportional differences in the projected death rates, even at adjacent ages, in the long run.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specifically, the projected mortality rates of LC are implausibly low for infants and younger ages relative to older ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This is in contrast to the findings in influential studies, including Li et al. [5], that found that mortality declines at younger ages have been slowing while declines at older ages have been accelerating.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A “rotation” approach of age-specific mortality decline speed was later proposed by Li et al. [5] to enhance the LC model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, this rotation is of an ad hoc nature rather than being data-driven [6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To address this, we investigate a time-varying coefficients extension of the LC model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Simply speaking, we employ a local constant kernel smoothing method [7] to model and forecast dynamic age-specific mortality declines.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this paper, we consider two commonly adopted kernel functions: Epanechnikov and Gaussian, and the corresponding extensions of the LC model are denoted by LC-E and LC-G, respectively.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Technical details of the modelling approach are provided, and our empirical results consider data of 15 low-mortality populations sourced from the famous Human Mortality Database [8], including annual mortality rates of age 0–100 spanning 1950–2019.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The contributions of this paper are threefold.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: First, the proposed time-varying coefficients extension of the LC model effectively complements the rotation adopted in Li et al. [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The proposed flexible framework ensures that the speed of rotation is data-driven, rather than ad hoc.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The existence of closed-form solutions further makes the proposed extension computationally efficient.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Secondly, using a comprehensive population dataset, we systematically demonstrate the outstanding performance of the time-varying models.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The overall superiority of the LC-E and LC-G models is robust when the age and temporal setting are changed.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The analysis of life expectancies up to 2100 further shows that the LC-G model can well address the issue of underestimated mortality improvements at old ages, existing for the LC model [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, the LC-E and LC-G models may provide potentially more accurate forecasts than the LC model in the research regarding long-term mortality projection.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, we describe the multi-population extensions of the employed models and illustrate their forecasting performances.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consistent with the single-population case, the newly proposed multi-population extensions are still overall the best performing model among all investigated specifications.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

## 2. Data and Methods

source_units.text:
The Lee–Carter and Related Models

Suppose we have mortality data of N ages, each age with T years of observations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The Lee–Carter (LC) model (1992) ([4]) summarizes the systematic mortality trends of the N ages by a common factor.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Formally, the log central mortality rate at age x in year t, lnmx,t, follows the specification given by:(1)lnmx,t=ax+bxkt+εx,t,
where ax is the mortality level, i.e., the average mortality rate over time at age x, kt is the period effect, i.e., the systematic mortality trend common to all ages, bx is the age effect at x, i.e., the sensitivity of lnmx,t to kt, and εx,t is the normal residual term with mean 0 and variance σεx2.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As noted by [4], Equation (1) is not identifiable without normalization constraints.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, one could multiply bx with a constant c and divide kt by the same constant and reach the same fitting results.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In [4], the following normalization constraints are imposed:∑tkt=0,and∑xbx=1
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
empty_or_punctuation_fragment

source_units.text: Given the constraint of kt, ax is set to the mean of lnmx,t over the sample considered.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The LC model is then estimated by singular value decomposition (SVD) instead of the usual ordinary least square approach in the original paper.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (A maximum likelihood estimation method may also be employed to calibrate the parameters [15].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alternatively, a Bayesian approach is proposed in Li et al. [16].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Compared to those estimation methods, SVD is much more computationally efficient and stable, which is critical to the proposed time-varying framework of this paper.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
)

While ax and bx are assumed to be constant, the period effect is often modeled by a time-series process.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
In particular, ref. [4] assumes a random walk with drift specification, which is adopted by many later studies:(2)kt=kt−1+d+et,
where the drift term d measures the average annual change in kt, and et∼i.i.d.N(0,σe2).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Based on the time-series specification in Equation (2), future mortality rates can be projected by extrapolating the period effect kt.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Specifically, the expected h-step-ahead mean forecasts of the period effect and the log central death rate are given by:(3)k^T+h=kT+hd,lnm^x,T+h=a^x+b^xk^T+h,
where T is the last year of the sample.

Issues with the Lee–Carter Model and Related Literature

For the long-spanning nature of mortality data, the static parametric structure of the LC model may not be compatible with reliable long-term demographic research.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To see this, the specification of the LC model decomposes mortality improvements into the product of latent non-stationary mortality trend factors (kt), assumed as a random walk with drift, and the corresponding age specific loadings of these trends (bx), assumed constant over time.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Considering the data displayed in Figure 1, we plot the fitted bx using a rolling window of a 30-year width in Figure 2. (There are no available data for the first 29 time points (i.e., 1950–1978) using the rolling window approach.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ) Clearly, the fitted bx becomes roughly “flatter” over time, with decreasing (increasing) weights for the younger (older) ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Ignoring such a dynamic pattern therefore reduces the credibility of the forecast mortality rates and life expectancies of LC.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Even when the BMS model is used, the static parametric nature is not necessarily sufficient to address this issue.

A Time-Varying Coefficients Extension of the Lee–Carter Model

To systematically address the ad hoc issue of Li et al. [5], we investigate a time-varying coefficients extension of the LC model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specifically, we employ a local constant kernel smoothing method [7], also known as the Nadaraya–Watson estimator, to accommodate the dynamics in the age-specific mortality declines.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A novel application of such an estimator in mortality forecasting can be found in Chang and Shi [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This approach allows bx to be time-dependent over both the in-sample (denoted by bx,t) and out-of-sample (denoted by bx,T+h) periods.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this paper, we consider two commonly adopted kernel functions: Epanechnikov and Gaussian, and the corresponding extensions of the LC model are denoted by LC-E and LC-G, respectively.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The technical details are described in this section.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

#### 2.4.1. A Time-Varying Framework Using Kernels

To incorporate the time-varying coefficients, we extend the LC model as follows:(4)lnmx,t=ax+bx,tkt+εx,t,
such that the age-specific declines are allowed to be dynamic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This suggests that the relative age-specific mortality decline speed is now time-dependent.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
In terms of the forecasting, we have that
(5)lnm^x,T+h=a^x+b^x,T+hk^T+h,
where b^x,T+h is the forecast bx,t at step h, and k^T+h is identically defined as in Equation (3).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consequently, to obtain forecasts of this time-varying framework, one needs to additionally model and forecast the time-dependent bx,t.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (Note that we do not require the assumption bx,t>0.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Negative values mean that mortality rates at certain ages may (temporarily) increase (relative to other ages), rather than decline.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As explained above, since this paper works with low-mortality populations, consistent declines are expected and more likely to occur.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For the estimation of the time-varying bx,t, many effective methods have been discussed in the statistics literature, including polynomial splines [20,21], smoothing splines [22,23], and kernel-local polynomial smoothing [24].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Among them, one of the most widely used methods is the kernel-local polynomial smoothing, which includes the local constant and the local linear estimation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this paper, we illustrate our method using the local constant kernel smoothing method [7], also known as the Nadaraya–Watson estimator.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To implement the estimation, at each time t, the usual SVD will be applied once to Kb(τs−τ)lnmx,s, where s=1,2,...,T, τ=t/T and τs=s/T. The resulting estimated “weighted” age-specific declines will be the corresponding b^x,t.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, Kb(τs−τ) is a known kernel function with b known as the bandwidth, and Kb(τs−τ) is essentially a weight for the sth observation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
For instance, with the widely employed Gaussian kernel, we have that
Kb(τs−τ)=12πbe−[(τs−τ)/b]22
which is essentially the Gaussian density evaluated at (τs−τ)/b and further scaled by b.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The bandwidth b then determines the weights distributed to each observation when estimating bx,t.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A larger b means weights are more evenly distributed.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Other than the Gaussian kernel, we also examine the popular Epanechnikov kernel in this paper, which is specified as
Kb(τs−τ)=0.75b{1−[(τs−τ)/b]2}+.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This kernel is also investigated in various mortality research, including Chang and Shi [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In this paper, we denote the time-varying coefficients LC model estimated by the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels as LC-G and LC-E, respectively.

Coherent Modelling of the Dynamic Age-Specific Mortality Declines To adjust b^x,t, we require that forecast mortality rates across ages will not diverge in the long run. This idea, known as age coherence, is much in-line with the rotation argued in Li et al. [5] and is critical to producing biologically reasonable forecasts of mortality rates in the long-term analysis [6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The age coherence is formally defined as follows.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To accommodate the age coherence in mortality forecasting, it is worth noting that lnmx,t is usually assumed to be a non-stationary I(1) process (see, for example, [6,19,28,29,30], among others).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, let yx,t=lnmx,t−lnmx,t−1, which is known as the mortality improvement of age x at time t, its long-run mean must be time-independent due to the stationarity.

It can then be shown that
lnm^x,T+h=E(lnmx,T+h|ΩT)=lnmx,T+∑k=1hE(yx,T+k|ΩT)=Op(1)+hμ^x
when h goes large, where ΩT is the information set at time T.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Hence, we denote this sequence by bx,t*, an appropriate parametric structure analogous to that discussed in Li and Lu [6] and described below.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

(6)b1,t*=α1b1,t−1*+ε1,tbb2,t*=α2b2,t−1*+β2b1,t−1*+ε2,tbbi,t*=αibi,t−1*+βibi−1,t−1*+γibi−2,t−1*+εi,tb
where i=3,...,N, and t=1,...,T. Essentially, Equation (6) is a vector autoregressive (VAR) model with constrained coefficient matrix.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to Li and Lu [6], the constraint is to emphasize the impact of the temporal effect (measured by αi) and those of the cohorts effect (measured by βi for the same cohort and γi for the nearest younger cohort).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

Tuning Parameters Selection and the Estimation Procedure

The only outstanding issue now is how to select the tuning parameters, i.e., smoothing penalties of the time-varying coefficients LC models.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In a usual case, a cross-validation technique can be employed to prevent the model from overfitting.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It is worth noting that a usual cross-validation technique for time-series data, such as the expanding-window approach explained in Hyndman and Athanasopoulos [31], is not quite applicable in our case.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The reason is that this expanding-window approach normally considers a very short forecasting step.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In contrast, age-coherent adjustment of the LC model emphasizes the long-term forecast.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Thus, we employ a hold-out-sample approach to select the tuning parameters (b and three λ’s), which minimizes
RMSFE=1N(T/3)∑i=1N∑h=1T/3lnm^i,2T/3+h−lnmi,2T/3+h2,
where RMSFE is the root of mean squared forecasting errors (since logged mortality rates are modeled, the RMSFE also considers the logged rather than original values.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: If an exponential transformation is applied, the predicted original mortality rates are unavoidably exposed to the famous Jensen’s inequality issue.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, the accuracy of forecasting is inherently lower than the logged rate is considered), and the evaluation period is given by the last third ([2T/3,T]) of the data in our study.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: (Note that the choice of the length of the test sample (one-third) is common among existing studies.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Adopting other popular alternatives, such as the last fourth, fifth, and tenth sample will lead to robust results.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
)

In summary, forecasting with the LC-E and LC-G models can be implemented with the following steps:Fit the original LC model with the full sample to obtain a^x, k^T, and d;For the training sample spanning [1,2T/3−1], use the Epanechnikov (LC-E) or Gaussian (LC-G) kernel to obtain bx,t, based on which the constrained VAR model of Equation (6) is fitted for bx,t*;Select the optimal tuning parameters b, λα, λβ, and λγ via a grid search, such that the RMSFE of the test sample over [2T/3,T] is minimized;With the selected tuning parameters, fit the LC-E or LC-G model for the full sample;Forecast b^x,T+h with the fitted model, and then produce lnm^x,T+h with Equation (5), where a^x and k^T+h=k^T+hd sourced from Step 1.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To study the uncertainties of the forecast, the same procedure of the LC model can be applied for the LC-E and LC-G models proposed in this section.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For instance, assuming that et in Equation (2) follows a Gaussian distribution, the prediction interval (PI) of the estimated life expectancies will be produced based on simulations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: More specifically, we use method (I) described in Li [32] to implement the simulation, and a 95% PI is then comprises the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the simulated results.

Extensions to the Multi-Population Modelling: An Illustrative Example

A multi-population extension of the LC model is studied in the seminal work of Li and Lee [9].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An additional common factor which controls the relationships between populations is included in the proposed Li–Lee (LL) model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
Specifically, the logged mortality rate is modeled as:(8)lnmx,t,j=ax,j+BxKt+bx,jkt,j+εx,t,j,
where ax,j represents the average of the age-specific mortality level for the jth population, Bx and Kt represent the age effect and period effect of the common factor, kt,j is the time component of the ith population with age response bx,j, and εx,t,j is the population-specific error term.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The common factor BxKt describes the mortality trend of all modeled populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To obtain the estimates, in this paper, we follow Li and Lee [9] to apply a usual LC model to the logged mortality rates averaged over all the fifteen populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consistent with LC, a^x,j is the average of lnmx,t,j over t.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The population-specific factor bx,ikt,i can be estimated by applying SVD to the residual matrix (lnmx,t,j−a^x,j−B^xK^t).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Similar to the case under LC, the common mortality index Kt is assumed non-stationary and can be modeled as a random walk with drift process.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In contrast, the group-specific time component kt,i is fitted by a stationary autoregressive process (set to AR(1) in this paper, as considered in Li and Lee [9]), such that long-term forecasts are coherent (i.e., non-divergent) across the included populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Given the data observed in the last year T, the h-step-ahead forecast of the logged mortality rate is given as follows:(9)lnm^x,T+h,j=a^x,j+B^xK^T+h+b^x,jk^T+h,j.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite its desirable coherence among populations, lnm^x,T+h,j of the LL model is still not age coherent.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To see this, without identical B^x across ages, the non-stationary temporal term K^T+h in Equation (9) can lead to divergent long-run forecasts even for neighboring ages of the same population.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The multi-population extensions of the BMS, LC-E, and LC-G are straightforward to derive.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Essentially, instead of fitting an LC model to forecast the common trend B^xK^T+h, BMS, LC-E, and LC-G models can be fitted for the averaged rates.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consequently, forecasts of their multi-population extensions can be produced below.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text:
(10)lnm^x,T+h,jB=a^x,j+B^xK^T+hB+b^x,jk^T+h,jlnm^x,T+h,jE=a^x,j+B^x,T+hEK^T+h+b^x,jk^T+h,jlnm^x,T+h,jG=a^x,j+B^x,T+hGK^T+h+b^x,jk^T+h,j
where the superscripts B, E, and G indicate the forecast of the multi-population extension of the BMS (LL-BMS), LC-E (LL-E), and LC-G (LL-G), respectively.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It can be seen that in all cases, the population-specific average rate a^x,j and stationary trend b^x,jk^T+h,j are unchanged from that of the LL model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For the LL-BMS, the same two adjustments, selecting an optimal sample period and using a Poisson model to obtain K^T+hB, as considered in the single-population BMS model are adopted for the averaged population.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For the LL-E and LL-G models, B^x,T+hE and B^x,T+hG will be forecast using the constrained VAR model as for the single-population case described in Equation (6), based on the averaged population.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The tuning parameters will be selected in the same way as described in Section 2.4.3, which will minimize the RMSFE of the averaged population for the hold-out sample.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Without imposing a long-run restriction, LL-BMS will lead to population-coherent forecasts as the LL, which are, however, not age coherent when h→∞.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In contrast, following the discussions in Section 2.4, B^x,T+hE and B^x,T+hG are age invariant in the long run.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Since k^T+h,j is a stationary process, b^x,jk^T+h,j will converge to a constant for all ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, the logged mortality rates forecast by LL-E and LL-G are both age- and population-coherent in the long run across all ages and populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: To effectively resolve this issue without imposing computationally intensive burdens, we employ the kernel time-varying parametric approach as examined in a recent work of Chang and Shi [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The forecasting of logged mortality rates is therefore conducted analogously to that for the LC model.

source_units.text: For the proposed LC-E and LC-G models, we can draw five key conclusions in this paper.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: First, the long-run age-specific patterns of mortality declines are forced (asymptotically) identical across all ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This ensures the desirable age coherence as proposed in the recent literature [6,19,28,29].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Second, the LC-E and LC-G models are computationally efficient and data-driven.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Specifically, both models adopt the penalized least square, which results in closed-form solutions.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, the parameters and smoothing penalties relevant to the speeds of rotation in b^x,T+h are estimated/determined in a data-driven fashion, which is different from the ad hoc judgment of the rotation used in Li et al. [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thirdly, using a large sample of uni-sex data of 15 countries over 1950–2019, we demonstrate the outstanding out-of-sample forecasting performance of the LC-E and LC-G models.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The differences in the selection of the kernel function is deemed marginal.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This conclusion is robust when a five-year instead of a one-year age mortality rate is modeled, and the training period is shortened to 1970–2000.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therefore, we recommend modelling and forecasting mortality rates with the time-varying coefficients LC model in demographic practices.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Fourthly, our long-term analysis supports the effectiveness of the age-coherent forecasts produced by the recommended model.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: When forecast to 2100, significantly longer life expectancies at birth are generated by the LC-G model in most illustrated cases, which may be caused by its larger forecast mortality improvements at old ages.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Finally, multi-population extensions of the LC-E (LL-E) and LC-G (LL-G) are straightforward to derive, which are based on the specification of the Li–Lee (LL) model Li and Lu [9].

source_units.text: There are some directions that are worth examining for future research.

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
